title: Instant Burst Capacity — Launch Messaging & Competitive Notes
audience: Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, Product Marketing, Partner GTM
exec_summary: Instant Burst is a new Dedicated capability that lets reserved-capacity customers temporarily exceed their committed GPUs with low-friction, SLA-aware bursts billed as short-term burst units. Target early adopters: gaming, retail, seasonal SaaS, and finance customers who experience predictable or unpredictable traffic spikes and need millisecond tail latencies during bursts. This doc contains messaging, competitive notes, pricing sketches, launch timeline, and an internal enablement checklist.
problem_statement: Customers on reserved Dedicated contracts face two hard trade-offs during spikes: over-provision (waste money) or risk throttling/fallback to lower-quality model variants (degraded UX). Existing autoscaling approaches are either too slow to meet latency SLOs or require complex ops work. We need a product-level capability that provides frictionless short-duration capacity above commit with predictable cost and consistent latency guarantees.
feature_one_liner: Seamlessly and instantly scale beyond your committed Dedicated capacity for short windows with SLA-aware routing and pay-per-burst billing.
key_messages: Keep your app tight under load: instant capacity increases with millisecond tail-latency guarantees during bursts.
Cost predictability: burst units are metered separately so customers only pay for time and compute used during peak windows.
Low-friction ops: enable via a toggle or API, integrate with existing autoscaling policies and rollouts; no infra changes required.
Safe and controlled: configurable caps, per-customer burst limits, and automatic fallback to committed capacity when policy thresholds are reached.
Compatible with Private and Dedicated: supports VPC-private deployments where possible (region and partner-dependent).
SLA-backed experience: burst sessions inherit Redwood latency SLOs for the selected model tier.
persona_bullets: Engineering leads: avoid last-minute infra purchases; reduce incident toil during peak events; keep consistent latency for users.
Platform/Infra teams: single control plane to manage commit and burst policies; audit logs for burst usage and governance.
Product managers for consumer apps (gaming, commerce): capture revenue during peaks without degradations or model fallbacks.
Finance/Procurement: pay only for peak increments without multi-month GPU commitments; clear burst unit metering simplifies forecasting.
Customer Success: easy upsell path from Dedicated to higher burst quotas for predictable revenue.
competitive_comparison: Cloud providers: GCP/Azure/AWS offer autoscaling VM pools, but autoscaling latency is tied to instance startup times and network cold starts; they lack token-level latency SLOs for LLM inference and per-request model fallbacks. Open-source runtimes: require significant SRE investment to implement burst-friendly routing, opaque cost-tracking, and no SLA. Vendors with hosted inference often only offer rate-limits or lower-priority burst lanes without committed latency guarantees. Instant Burst differentiates by combining predictable billing, millisecond latency SLOs for bursts, integration with existing Dedicated contracts, and first-class observability (token-level cost/latency breakdown during burst windows).
pricing_snippet: Burst units billed hourly-per-GPU-equivalent with tiered discounts for committed customers. Example sketch: base Dedicated commit charged as today; bursts charged at 2.5x committed per-GPU-hour with metering in 1-minute increments. Pre-purchased burst credits available for large customers with term discounts. Billing details and metering docs owned by finance-pricing team (linked artifact JIRA-INV-4321).
launch_timeline: Week 0: Feature sign-off and pricing approval
Week 1-2: Documentation freeze - API spec, Console UX, billing matrix
Week 3: SE enablement workshop + internal dry-run with test accounts
Week 4: Private beta with 3 anchor customers (gaming, retail, fintech)
Week 6: Feedback iteration and SLA fine-tuning
Week 8: Public launch + sales enablement kit release

sample_announcement:
Headline: Instant Burst — Handle traffic spikes without over-provisioning
Subhead: Temporarily scale beyond your Dedicated capacity with SLA-aware bursts and pay-for-what-you-use pricing.
Body preview: Today we’re launching Instant Burst, a Dedicated capability that lets teams handle short windows of intense demand without buying extra GPUs long term. Turn on burst in the Console or call the Burst API, and your requests will be routed to extra capacity with the same latency guarantees you expect from Redwood. Try a 30-day pilot with our launch partners and get a burst credit to validate your peak workloads.
internal_faq: Q: Will bursts affect other customers in the same region? A: No — bursts use isolated burst pools and scheduling policies with fairness windows; capacity is managed by Instant Burst orchestration to prevent noisy neighbor effects.

Q: How do we ensure latency SLOs when bursting? A: Burst sessions are served by pre-warmed GPU pools and prioritized routing; we maintain the same attention kernels and KV cache semantics to minimize cold-start overhead.
Q: Is Instant Burst available in Private deployments? A: Supported for VPC-hosted Dedicated in regions where partner co-located burst capacity is available; see confluence link for per-region status.
Q: How are burst failures surfaced? A: Console shows real-time burst health and fallback events; customers receive structured webhooks and audit logs for each burst session.
Q: Can burst usage be predicted or auto-trigged? A: Yes — customers can attach thresholds and external triggers (webhook/metrics) to auto-initiate bursts; predictive triggers are a roadmap item.
Q: What happens if burst capacity is exhausted? A: Requests revert to committed capacity and follow configured fallback policies (lower throughput, model fallback, queued requests).
